rendered: After sulfur infiltration, the D peak red-shifts by 17[1] cm-1. On discharge, the D peak shows a further redshift of 12[2] cm-1 relative to the as-prepared electrode (the paper gives the D and G peak redshifts as 12[3] and 14[4] cm-1 respectively). The total red shift of the D peak that the paper states is >25 wavenumbers[5], arising from the combination of sulfur infiltration and sodiation. The paper does not state the discharge increment as a single subtracted value, and the discharge shift is measured against the as-prepared electrode rather than the infiltrated carbon, so the figures are not strictly additive.
